Aisha (support): FYI customer 'BrightScope' just escalated — p99 latency went from ~220ms -> 1.2s after we enabled a new quant profile on their dedicated instance. They're seeing timeouts in production.
Tom (sre): :eyes: Which profile did they flip to and when?
Aisha (support): int8_profile_2026-03-14 applied at 09:02 UTC. Model is rwd-v1-3b (server variant rwd-3b-dedicated-2). Metrics show p95 ~270ms (ok) but p99 jump to ~1.2s, increased tokenization time + per-token overhead.
Ravi (ml): Do we have any stack traces/log lines from the runtime? Could be slower kernels or a fallback path being triggered.
Aisha (support): They attached logs. Snippet: ```[2026-03-14T09:02:05Z] quant_profile: applied int8_profile_2026-03-14
[2026-03-14T09:02:06Z] layer12: quant_calib: profile missing -> entering calibration mode (sync)
[2026-03-14T09:02:06Z] runtime: dequantize_slow_path invoked (per-step)
[2026-03-14T09:02:07Z] serve: request id=... latency=980ms tokens=120```
Jules (platform): That "calibration mode (sync)" line is worrying — looks like per-worker on-demand calibration is happening which can be blocking. We recently changed fallback behavior: when a missing per-layer calibration is detected we do a sync calibration rather than async background calibrate.
Tom (sre): If calibration is sync, first few inferences will spike. But p99 sustained suggests repeated slow paths, maybe cache misses or KV cache incompatibility after quant change. Are clients reusing same sessions/streams?
Aisha (support): Customer confirms no connection drop — they reuse streaming connections. They report spikes across many requests, not just first few.
Ravi (ml): Two hypotheses: (1) quant profile introduced a different block layout causing our kernel selector to pick slower kernels for certain sequence lengths; (2) calibration incomplete -> frequent dequant/quant roundtrips because cached KV format differs between int8 and fp16 cached entries.
Jules (platform): Quick mitigation options: (a) roll profile back to prior profile (fp16_profile_v2) on that dedicated pool; (b) enable fp16 fallback for that endpoint via route config; (c) flip runtime flag quant.runtime.allow_sync_calib=false to force async calibration. Which can we do fast?
Tom (sre): (a) rollback is fastest. We can revert the profile on the customer's pool in ~2 min. (b) enabling fp16 fallback needs a config push but low risk, ~5-10 min. (c) runtime flag requires a restart of worker processes (~10-12 min).
Aisha (support): Customer asking for immediate fix — prefers rollback. They want postmortem and safe re-try plan for a later calibration.
Ravi (ml): For postmortem we should capture: a) kernel selection logs, b) quant layer mapping + which layers failed to find calibration, c) KV cache format version on active workers, d) sample requests that hit p99. Also check if batch size or sequence length distribution changed after profile because that can change kernel choice.
Aisha (support): I've collected these and attached to the case: kernel_selector.log, quant_layer_report.txt, kv_cache_versions.json, sample_requests.ndjson.
Tom (sre): I'll trigger rollback now on rwd-3b-dedicated-2 pool and mark in incident channel.
quant-bot: deploy-bot: rollback quant profile int8_profile_2026-03-14 -> fp16_profile_v2 applied to pool rwd-3b-dedicated-2 by tom at 2026-03-14T09:08:12Z
Aisha (support): After rollback customer reports p99 back to ~240ms, errors cleared. :thumbsup:
Ravi (ml): Good. Next steps before re-applying a quant profile to this customer's pool: 1) run offline per-layer calibration simulator against their production prompt set to produce a complete calibration artifact (no missing layers), 2) run kernel selection smoke tests for their seq length distribution, 3) run KV cache compatibility check between fp16 and int8 cache formats and implement a one-time migrate or cache invalidation on rollout.
Jules (platform): Also add a safety gate: if more than X% of requests in the last 10m hit sync calibration path, abort rollout automatically and revert.
Tom (sre): I've filed infra ticket INF-6123 to add the abort-on-sync-calib gate.
Aisha (support): Customer accepted rollback and asked for a safe relaunch plan. I'm proposing a canary: enable int8 on 5% of nodes + async-only calibration + pre-warm cache (run replay of top 2k requests) before increasing to 100%.
Ravi (ml): Sounds right. For the calibration artifact generation, run this locally: ```python repro_calib.py --model rwd-v1-3b --prompts brightscope_prompts.ndjson --target-profile=auto --output=calib-int8-2026-03-14.bin``` That produces a full-layer calibration file that we can push with the profile.
Jules (platform): Also ask customer to disable any per-request profile header toggles during the canary so they don't accidentally override pool settings.
Aisha (support): I'll send the plan and schedule a maintenance window.
Tom (sre): Postmortem owners: Aisha (support) to lead customer comms, Ravi (ml) to own calibration artifacts and kernel tests, Jules (platform) to own rollout gating and infra changes, Tom (sre) to verify rollback automation.
Aisha (support): Thanks everyone. Closing the urgent escalated path for now. Will loop with customer once the safe plan is ready.
Ravi (ml): Follow-ups: we'll check whether fp8 profile has similar risks — fp8 uses different quant scales and could interact with kernels differently. I'll add fp8 compatibility tests to the reproduction matrix.
Aisha (support): Noted. Closing thread. :white_check_mark:
